paragraphs: A catcher's mask is a steel cage on a padded frame, and the cage is the whole object: bars arranged so a ball cannot pass but the eye line stays clear, which is a genuinely difficult geometry problem and the reason no two designs look alike. The harness straps and the throat guard complete it.

The mesh is efficient at 17,666 polygons and 17,610 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with almost all of that count in the cage bars where the shape has to be real rather than textured.

At $39 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits baseball and sports visualisation, broadcast graphics, sporting goods retail renders, character set dressing and games. Real-world scale is kept, so it fits a standard head. On sale since 2024.

The Benin heads are among the finest metal castings ever made anywhere, produced by lost wax in a court workshop tradition going back centuries. The style is unmistakable: a stylised face with high relief coral bead collar rising to the chin, scarification marks above the eyes and a smooth polished dome.
The mesh runs 38,927 polygons and 39,173 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the beadwork and the facial features where the casting detail lives.

At $39 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits museum and exhibition visualisation, African art and history material, cultural heritage presentation, education content, gallery and interior renders, and games. On sale since 2024.

An OBD scan tool is a handheld with a screen, a keypad and a thick cable ending in a trapezoid connector. That connector shape is standardised across every car built for decades, and it is the detail that identifies the tool immediately to anyone who has plugged one in under a dashboard.
The mesh is light at 9,427 polygons and 10,002 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the keypad, the screen bezel and the connector.
At $39 it suits automotive workshop and service visualisation, diagnostic equipment marketing, garage interiors, technician training material and games. On sale since 2021.

A curved dolly track lets a camera orbit a subject at a fixed radius, which is one of the few moves that cannot be faked convincingly by hand. The track sections lock together into a ring, sit on adjustable feet to level on uneven ground, and the trolley rides on them with the camera or a operator platform on top.
The mesh runs 131,502 polygons and 131,258 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the rail profile, the joining hardware and the trolley wheels.

At $39 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits film and television production visualisation, studio and location set dressing, rental house and equipment catalogues, behind the scenes illustration and games. On sale since 2025.

This chassis ships flat and folds into a computer case, which is the whole design argument: the panels are pre-cut and scored, the user bends them along the creases and locks them together. Shown unfolded, the object explains itself in a way that no photograph of the finished box can.
The mesh runs 239,044 polygons and 236,871 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, with the density in the punched vent patterns and the fold lines that make the flat pack readable.

At $39 and built to StemCell specification, it suits product and industrial design presentation, technology and maker marketing, packaging and flat pack visualisation, editorial imagery and games. On sale since 2026.

A confessional is a piece of church joinery with a very particular arrangement: a central compartment for the priest, side compartments for the penitent, a screen between them and a curtain or door on each side. Shown open, the interior becomes visible, which is what makes the object comprehensible rather than a decorated cabinet.
The mesh runs 198,737 polygons and 132,243 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the panelling, the mouldings and the screen tracery.

At $39 and built to StemCell specification, it suits ecclesiastical and heritage interior visualisation, film and television set dressing, historical and religious material, architectural renders and games. On sale since 2024.

A croquet set is a small collection of very specific objects: mallets with long handles and cylindrical heads, hard balls in four colours, wire hoops and a centre peg. The mallets are the recognisable part, and their proportion is what separates the game from anything played with a stick and a ball.
The mesh is light at 37,430 polygons and 18,967 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the pieces modelled separately so they can be laid out, stacked or placed on a lawn.
At $39 it suits garden and outdoor leisure visualisation, hospitality and country house imagery, lifestyle and summer advertising, period film and television, and games. On sale since 2024.

A curling sheet is mostly painted ice: the house with its concentric circles at each end, the hog lines, the centre line and the hacks the players push off from. Those markings under the ice are the whole visual, which is why the surface has to be modelled as a proper sheet rather than as a flat plane.

The model is built with subdivision geometry at 11,988 polygons and 12,553 vertices with non-overlapping UVs, which is the right approach for a venue whose interest is the surface rather than the structure.
At $39 it suits winter sports broadcast graphics, curling and olympic material, venue and event visualisation, sports advertising and games. On sale since 2021.

The ordering kiosk changed the layout of fast food restaurants more than anything since the drive through. It is a tall column with a large touchscreen at standing height, a card reader below and a receipt slot at the bottom, and it stands in the middle of the floor rather than at a counter.
The mesh is light at 13,895 polygons and 13,957 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the screen as a separate surface so an interface image goes on without masking.
At $39 it suits restaurant and retail interior visualisation, hospitality technology marketing, store planning presentation, film and television set dressing, and games. On sale since 2021.

The New York hydrant is a specific object rather than a generic one: a squat body, a bonnet with a pentagon operating nut, one large steamer connection facing the street and two smaller side outlets. Its colour and its dents are as much a part of the streetscape as the traffic light or the manhole cover.

The mesh runs 30,085 polygons and 30,961 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 9 texture maps at a mix of sizes up to 4096x4096 carrying the chipped paint, the rust and the road salt staining.
At $39 it suits urban and street visualisation, film and television set dressing, architectural exteriors, emergency services material and games. On sale since 2016.

A portable air conditioner is a box on castors with a fat exhaust hose out of the back, and that hose is what gives the product away: it has to reach a window, which is why the unit always sits near one and why the hose is such a visible part of the object rather than something hidden.
The mesh runs 78,112 polygons and 43,075 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the vent louvres, the control panel and the castors.
At $39 it suits interior and residential visualisation, appliance retail and e-commerce renders, office and home scenes, HVAC marketing and games. On sale since 2023.

A modular floating pontoon is built from identical cubes that clip together, which means the same product can become a jetty, a swimming platform or a boat lift depending on how many are joined and in what shape. That modularity is the selling point, and it means the single unit has to tile perfectly.

The mesh runs 24,052 polygons and 24,722 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 8 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the moulded plastic and the algae staining at the waterline.
At $39 it suits marina and waterfront visualisation, marine equipment marketing, resort and hospitality renders, watersports material and games. On sale since 2018.

A juice dispenser is a glass fronted cabinet with transparent bowls turning inside it, each with a paddle that keeps the liquid moving so it does not separate. That visible movement is the marketing: the machine exists to show the product as much as to serve it, which is why the bowls face the customer.
The mesh runs 104,966 polygons and 106,420 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the bowls as separate transparent bodies so a liquid material can be applied properly.
At $39 it suits food service and hospitality visualisation, cafe and buffet interiors, catering equipment marketing, retail and convenience scenes, and games. On sale since 2021.

The first generation of this phone had a distinctive two-tone back: a glass panel over the upper third and metal below it, with the fingerprint sensor centred in the glass. That split is the identifying feature of the generation, and it disappeared from later models entirely.

The mesh is light at 20,214 polygons and 21,322 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 6 texture maps at a mix of sizes up to 4096x4096 carrying the glass, the anodised metal and the screen.
At $39 it suits consumer electronics visualisation, product and e-commerce renders, technology journalism and archive material, desk and interior scenes, and games. On sale since 2017.
